models_evaluated: deep neural network cervical image quality classifier

links.outcome: Image quality classifier performance across devices and geographies, internal vs external validation
links.effect: Internal AUROC 0.92 (LQ) and 0.93 (HQ), %EM 2.8%; external different-device set AUROC 0.83 and 0.82, %EM 3.9%; no meaningful difference across geographies.
links.quote: Our model also generalized well externally, achieving corresponding AUROCs of 0.83 and 0.82, and %EM of 3.9% when tested out-of-the-box on the external validation (“EXT”) set.

links.outcome: Performance degradation (catastrophic forgetting) after retraining with new data
links.effect: No catastrophic forgetting upon retraining with new data; no meaningful performance difference across geographies.
links.quote: Additionally, our model was geography agnostic with no meaningful difference in performance across geographies, did not exhibit catastrophic forgetting upon retraining with new data, and mimicked the overall/average ground truth rater behavior well.

unlisted_practices: Automated image quality control classifier as a guardrail upstream of diagnostic AI
Assessing impact of ground-truth rater variability on model performance

screen.reason: The study develops and benchmarks an image quality classification model intended as a guardrail/quality filter for cervical imaging pipelines, but it evaluates the model's accuracy on internal and external datasets rather than testing an intervention with/without a deployment practice.
